outcome: bacterial distribution in blood and chorioamniotic swab cultures
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 419 women attempting vaginal delivery at a tertiary hospital who were diagnosed with intrapartum fever between 2010 and 2022.
finding: Women with maternal bacteremia had higher rates of endometritis, lower Apgar scores at 5 minutes, lower umbilical cord pH, and higher NICU admission rates, with prolonged ROM and prophylactic ampicillin being linked to maternal bacteremia.
